measured: Baseline passed 56 of 100 tools tasks; noop and rollback also passed 56 of 100 and produced reply text identical to baseline on 100 of 100 tasks each.

ffn_med passed 19 of 100 (43 tasks regressed from baseline, 6 improved) and ffn_up_low passed 24 of 100 (35 regressed, 3 improved); ffn_low passed 55, attn_low 58, attn_med 52, rand_ffn_med 49 and rand_attn_med 49.

Against its matched random control, ffn_med failed 37 tasks that rand_ffn_med passed and passed 7 that rand_ffn_med failed (19 versus 49 of 100); attn_med failed 12 that rand_attn_med passed and passed 15 that it failed (52 versus 49 of 100).
Episodes that ended with no final answer inside the step limit: baseline 14, ffn_low 3, attn_low 10, attn_med 30, ffn_med 47, ffn_up_low 51, rand_ffn_med 15, rand_attn_med 10 (each out of 100).

Episodes with at least one reply that was not a valid protocol JSON object: baseline 8, ffn_low 16, ffn_med 63, ffn_up_low 9, attn_low 5, attn_med 4, rand_ffn_med 32, rand_attn_med 14; total such replies were 10 at baseline and 150 under ffn_med.

By task batch, ffn_med passed 0 of the 20 calc tasks (tool-021 to tool-040; baseline 13, rand_ffn_med 14) and ffn_up_low passed 0 of the 20 edit tasks (tool-041 to tool-060; baseline 8); 23 tasks failed under all 10 conditions and 3 passed under all 10.
failure_patterns: Tool call followed in the same reply by a guessed final answer written before any tool result (the harness keeps only the first object): 15 of the 43 traces read, 10 of them failures. Across all episodes this appeared in 20 baseline, 57 ffn_low, 69 ffn_med, 0 ffn_up_low, 4 attn_med, 44 rand_ffn_med and 32 rand_attn_med episodes.

Answer given as bare text without the {"final": ...} wrapper, counted as a format error and often followed by re-calling the same tool until the step limit: 12 of 43 traces read had a non-JSON reply and 6 of those ended with no final. Across all episodes, 47 of the 47 ffn_med no-final episodes had at least one non-JSON reply.

Repeating an identical tool call with identical arguments, with every reply well formed, until the step limit: 5 of 43 traces read (16 of 43 had some repeated identical call). Across all episodes this well-formed loop with no final occurred in 10 baseline, 40 ffn_up_low, 27 attn_med and 0 ffn_med episodes.
Calling a tool name that does not exist (for example "list_files()", "DONE", "final", "kv_rename", "compare_files"): 5 of 43 traces read. Across all episodes: 6 baseline, 14 ffn_up_low, 2 ffn_med.

Running the calc example copied from the tool documentation, (3+4)*2, in place of the task's own numbers: 4 of 43 traces read. Across all episodes: 2 baseline, 13 ffn_med, 8 ffn_up_low. Separately, 5 of 43 traces read called a tool the task forbade; across all episodes that check failed in 9 baseline, 24 ffn_up_low and 2 ffn_med episodes.
surprises: ffn_med and ffn_up_low reached similar pass counts (19 and 24) with different trace shapes: ffn_med had 63 episodes with non-JSON replies and 0 well-formed repeat loops, ffn_up_low had 9 episodes with non-JSON replies and 40 well-formed repeat loops.
ffn_low had fewer no-final episodes than baseline (3 versus 14) while having more episodes with non-JSON replies (16 versus 8), and its pass count was 55 versus 56.
attn_med had 30 no-final episodes versus 14 at baseline yet passed 52 versus 56, and it passed 8 of 30 hard tasks versus 6 at baseline; rand_ffn_med also passed 8 hard tasks.
interpretation: The ffn_med drop on this family (19 versus 49 of 100 for the matched random control, 37 worse and 7 better) is larger than what the same-size random edit produced, so it does not look like an effect of change size alone; this is one model, one seed and 100 tasks, so it should be read as specific to this setup.

Most failures that separate ffn_med and ffn_up_low from baseline in the traces read look like protocol and stopping failures (non-JSON answers, repeated calls, no final) more than wrong lookups or arithmetic, but that reading rests on 43 traces plus automated counts and the scoring is all-or-nothing per task.
attn_low and attn_med pass counts (58 and 52) are within the baseline confidence interval reported in summary.json (0.46 to 0.65), so the data may not distinguish them from baseline on this family.
unknown: Whether the model would have reached the right answer with a more lenient protocol (for example accepting bare-text answers or a larger step limit); the data only shows pass or fail under the fixed harness.
Whether these counts would hold with a different random seed, sampling setting or a second random-sign control draw; each condition was run once per task.
Why ffn_med and ffn_up_low differ in trace shape; nothing in the episode records identifies a mechanism.

examples.label: representative
examples.why: Shows the bare-text pattern: calc returned 3024, the reply was the bare number three times with no final wrapper, ending with no final; chosen as a typical member of the 47 ffn_med no-final episodes, all of which had a non-JSON reply.

examples.label: representative
examples.why: Shows the well-formed repeat loop: kv_get then read_file returned the budget, then the same two calls repeated to the step limit with no final; chosen as typical of the 40 ffn_up_low episodes with that shape.

examples.label: representative
examples.why: Unchanged pass: calc errored on 'x', was retried with '*', and the final was correct, same outcome as baseline; chosen from the 3 tasks that passed under all 10 conditions to show an unaffected case.

examples.label: edge case
examples.why: An improvement under the condition with the fewest passes: the first reply contained a guessed final (12.5) after the tool call, the harness dropped it, and the next reply gave the correct 38; chosen from the 6 ffn_med improvements to show a pass that depends on the one-object rule.

examples.label: edge case
examples.why: A hard three-step key lookup that failed at baseline (it queried the literal keys 'depot_' and 'km_') and passed under ffn_up_low, which passed 24 of 100 overall; chosen from the 3 ffn_up_low improvements.

examples.label: failure
examples.why: kv_get on the same key six times, never sending the required message or a final; chosen from the 11 attn_med regressions as an instance of the 27 attn_med well-formed loop episodes.

examples.label: failure
examples.why: All tool steps and the written file were correct but the final was 'ok' in place of the sum, so only the number check failed; chosen from the 14 rand_ffn_med regressions to show that the matched control also regresses, in a different way.

examples.label: failure
examples.why: Called calc with '2537 Mod 24', got a syntax error, then answered 1 without retrying (correct remainder is 17); chosen from the 6 ffn_low regressions, a condition whose pass count was 55 versus 56 at baseline.
